China's $3.5 Trillion Stock Rout Deepens as Sinking Corporate Profits Outpace Stimulus Hopes

30 Oct 2026, 02:22 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.business-standard.com

Pessimism has gripped Chinese financial markets as a prolonged selloff erodes equity values, bringing the total market loss to $3.5 trillion since a peak in May, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The downturn has pushed the onshore benchmark CSI 300 Index into a bear market, while key technology indexes approach erasing gains accumulated since Beijing's previous support packages.

Earnings Pressures and Cut-Throat Competition

At the center of the investor downturn is a combination of a protracted domestic consumption slump and intense corporate rivalry. Analysts point to a race-to-the-bottom pricing mentality across multiple industries, affecting sectors ranging from traditional banking and electric vehicles to artificial intelligence model developers and green energy.

The third-quarter reporting season underscored these pressures. Prominent firms, including battery manufacturer Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL), reported profit misses driven by weak demand and fierce competition. Consensus 2026 earnings forecasts for members of the MSCI China Index have declined by more than 4% since late March, while the Hang Seng Tech Index has seen profit projections drop over 13%.

Furthermore, companies releasing third-quarter results missed consensus forecasts by an average of 9%. Major firms such as China Mobile Ltd. and Ganfeng Lithium Group Co. also reported earnings that fell short of estimates amid cost pressures and falling commodity prices.

Policy Stance and Market Response

Adding to investor caution is the perception that Chinese authorities are not planning aggressive fiscal intervention. Third-quarter gross domestic product grew by 4.5% from a year prior, placing the nine-month expansion within the government's annual target of 4.5% to 5%. Analysts note that this target-compliant performance allows policymakers to maintain a measured, drip-feed approach to economic support rather than implementing large-scale stimulus.

While state funds—often referred to as the "national team"—have intervened to stabilize prices and prevent disorderly drops, skepticism remains regarding long-term prospects without significant consumption-boosting measures.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

  • What is Confirmed: Chinese equities have experienced a $3.5 trillion decline from their May peak, leading the CSI 300 Index into a bear market. Third-quarter earnings have widely missed consensus estimates amid margin squeezes and intense industry competition. Official GDP growth stands within the government's 4.5% to 5% target range, leading to restrained fiscal stimulus.
  • What Remains Unknown: The duration of the corporate profit squeeze, the long-term effectiveness of state-backed market stabilization funds, and whether future policy shifts might alter consumer demand remain uncertain.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review original market data, corporate earnings reports, and official economic updates directly via the Business Standard Report.
